acceptance: A scheduled refresh pull request with an unrewritten bot commit is observed through one arm attempt after an owner stand-in, and the outcome is recorded with GitHub's merge state.
context:
Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).

Owner decision 2026-11-22 (choice dialog). Where it conflicts with the Decision gates text in the description, this wins. "If no refresh pull request opens, record why and hold the item to the following Monday." Roles unchanged: the owner posts any stand-in; the agent arms once.
description:
## Problem
This item first said the develop ruleset's unattributed-commit rule blocks refresh pull requests because they commit as `benchbox-bot <bot@benchbox.dev>`. Evidence read on 2026-11-20 does not support that: #3914, #3915, #4004, #4090 and #4317 each merged with a sole commit by that identity and no linked account; #4090 and #4317 merged under the ruleset version last changed on 2026-11-10; #4317 merged by auto-merge on 2026-11-18. None had an approving review. The scheduled refreshes that did not merge differ from each other: #4066 and #4283 were marked too large to review, so the required `review-gate` check waited for a stand-in that nobody posted; #3928 and medium-shard #4284 passed review (`review-gate` green; #4284 had a SHIP verdict) and were simply never armed. What they share is that nobody attended them. Why #4381's first head f734774a sat for 15 minutes with every required check green and auto-merge on (core green 16:29:30Z, force-push 16:45:20Z on 2026-11-19) is unexplained.

## Owner decision
Question: why refresh pull requests stall, and the bot identity. Chosen option, as the agent wrote it to the owner: "Recommended: leave the identity alone. Add only a visible failure when a scheduled refresh opens while the previous one is still open. On the next scheduled refresh (Monday 23 Nov) you post the stand-in, I arm once with no re-authoring, and we see whether it merges." In that text 'you' is the owner and 'I' is the agent. Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
No workflow identity change. The schedule is Mondays 06:17 UTC. When the scheduled fast-tier refresh pull request of 2026-11-23 opens, tell the owner its number and head and whether the review bot reviewed it. If it needs a stand-in, the owner posts it. Then the agent runs `make pr-arm` once and records what GitHub reports: merged, or blocked with the merge state and every required check's state.

## Decision gates
Held until 2026-11-23T17:00Z. A stand-in is the owner's to post, naming that pull request and head at the time; the agent never posts one. No agent re-authors, amends or force-pushes a refresh commit. If it does not merge, record the evidence and stop; a ruleset or identity change is owner-only.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the item records the pull request number, head, the commit author, the review bot's verdict, the stand-in comment's time if one was needed, the single `make pr-arm` output and the final state read from GitHub.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
